sources.title: Rational snacking: Young children’s decision-making on the marshmallow task is moderated by beliefs about environmental reliability
sources.why_it_matters: Proved in 28 children that broken vs kept adult promises before the Marshmallow Test changed average wait times fourfold (3 min 2 sec vs 12 min 2 sec).

sources.title: Cognitive and attentional mechanisms in delay of gratification.
sources.journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
sources.why_it_matters: Original Stanford Marshmallow delay-of-gratification paradigm establishing attentional distraction strategies during 15-minute solo waiting.

sources.title: Revisiting the Marshmallow Test: A Conceptual Replication Investigating Links Between Early Delay of Gratification and Later Outcomes
sources.why_it_matters: Replicated the Marshmallow Test in >900 diverse children, showing family stability and environment explain most of the later-life correlation once controls are added.

sources.title: Evidence accumulation, not ‘self-control’, explains dorsolateral prefrontal activation during normative choice
sources.why_it_matters: Demonstrated via human fMRI and computational modeling that dorsolateral and ventromedial prefrontal cortex accumulate expected value evidence rather than exerting mystical 'willpower'.

sources.title: Behavioral and neural correlates of delay of gratification 40 years later
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
sources.why_it_matters: Forty-year longitudinal fMRI follow-up of original Stanford Bing Nursery participants mapping inferior frontal gyrus vs ventral striatal reactivity.

sources.title: Delaying gratification depends on social trust
sources.why_it_matters: Independently demonstrated that adult social trustworthiness directly modulates children's willingness to delay gratification.
